newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds took their cue from positive U.S. economic data to go on a late afternoon rally which propelled them into positive territory.
The spread to Bunds remained fairly steady but the yield curve continued to steepen as the figures attracted sellers of longer dated state loans.
Guilder paper erased its losses as the market was cheered by U.S. producer price, industrial production, capacity utilisation and consumer sentiment data.
"Everything that came out today was good for the bond market," said one dealer.
She said interest in longer bonds increased when the market jumped after the figures, noting that she saw switching by several large international houses out of 2007 bonds into 2010s.
Outright selling of longer dates was also reported.
"It shows that people are long, higher up," she said.
Another dealer said demand for shorter to mid-curve paper had been seen in recent days as the guilder yield curve steepened.
"One or two accounts have tried to shorten on the curve. It's a defensive trading strategy," he said.
This was attributed to the Dutch guilder stabilising against the German mark after the Dutch central bank's decision to raise interest rates twice in two weeks.
The 10-2 year yield finished at 204 basis points (bp), a rise of six bp in the last three days, while the 10-5 spread was 88 bp, up three in the same period.
One trader also saw switching out of British gilts and Bunds into guilders, although the Dutch-German yield spread was barely changed.
The market had opened lower in response to a lower finish by U.S. Treasuries and remained there for much of the day.
